---
title: "Method and library reference"
author: "Mingyang Lu"
---

This closing chapter is a cheat sheet for the whole book. Each table maps a
computational task to its R and Python implementation and to the chapter where it
is developed. The idea behind a method is language-agnostic, so the two
implementation columns are meant to be read side by side: pick the language you
work in, and use the other column to translate.

**How to read the tables.** A name in `monospace` is a function *defined from
scratch in the book* (the method is built up so you understand it, not called as a
black box). A name written as `package::function` or as a library (for example
`scipy.integrate`) is a standard library used where it is the practical choice. Many
tasks appear in both forms: the book first builds the method by hand, then points to
the library you would reach for in practice. The final table lists the R and Python
libraries used throughout, as a quick translation guide.

## Programming foundations (Part 1)

| Task | R | Python | Chapter |
|------|-----|--------|:--:|
| Functions, control flow, vectorization | base R | `numpy`, base Python | [1A](01-intro/01a-getting-started.qmd) |
| Timing and benchmarking | `microbenchmark` | `timeit` | [1B](01-intro/01b-efficient-programming.qmd) |
| Speeding up code (compilation / JIT) | `compiler`, vectorization | `numba` (`@njit`) | [1B](01-intro/01b-efficient-programming.qmd) |
| Calling compiled code | `.Fortran` / `dyn.load` | `ctypes` | [1B](01-intro/01b-efficient-programming.qmd) |
| Parallel execution | `parallel::mclapply` | `multiprocessing` (fork) | [1B](01-intro/01b-efficient-programming.qmd) |
| A first numerical method (`babylonian` square root) | from scratch | from scratch | [1C](01-intro/01c-numerical-methods.qmd) |
| Parsing a protein structure | `bio3d` | `Bio.PDB` (`biopython`) | [1D](01-intro/01d-exercises.qmd) |

## R and Python library map

The libraries used across the book, grouped by domain.

| Domain | R | Python |
|--------|-----|--------|
| ODE solving | `deSolve` (`ode`, `dede`) | `scipy.integrate` (`odeint`, `solve_ivp`) |
| Root finding and optimization | `rootSolve` (`uniroot.all`, `multiroot`), `stats` (`uniroot`, `optim`, `nlm`, `nls`, `lm`) | `scipy.optimize` (`fsolve`, `minimize`, `curve_fit`) |
| Linear algebra, eigenvalues | base (`eigen`, `svd`, `solve`) | `numpy.linalg` (`eig`, `eigvals`, `svd`, `solve`) |
| Plotting | `ggplot2`, base graphics | `matplotlib.pyplot` |
| Animation | `gganimate` (+ `gifski`) | `matplotlib.animation` |
| Data frames and tables | `data.frame`, `knitr::kable` | `pandas` |
| Benchmarking | `microbenchmark` | `timeit` |
| Compiled / just-in-time code | `compiler`, `.Fortran` / `dyn.load` | `numba` (`@njit`), `ctypes` |
| Parallelism | `parallel` (`mclapply`) | `multiprocessing` |
| Dimensionality reduction | `Rtsne`, `uwot`, `princurve`, base (`prcomp`, `cmdscale`) | `scikit-learn` (`decomposition`, `manifold`), `umap-learn`, `pcurvepy2` |
| Clustering | `stats` (`kmeans`, `hclust`), `mclust` | `scikit-learn` (`cluster`, `mixture`), `scipy.cluster.hierarchy` |
| Networks | `igraph` | `networkx` |
| Structural biology | `bio3d` | `biopython` (`Bio.PDB`) |
